title: Kirk Cousins Set as Raiders' Starting QB vs. Jets, Says Klint Kubiak – ESPN Report
body:
The Las Vegas Raiders confirmed on Monday that veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins will stay under center for Sunday’s road game against the New York Jets, ending weeks of speculation about a possible benching. Head coach Klint Kubiak made the decision clear, emphasizing that there is “no controversy” surrounding Cousins’ role and that the team will continue to ride the 38‑year‑old signal‑caller as its primary offensive leader.

Cousins, who was acquired in a trade from the Minnesota Vikings during the offseason, entered the season as the Raiders’ most experienced passer, expected to bring stability to a unit that struggled to find consistency last year. Over the first six weeks, he has posted a 3‑3 record, completing 64 percent of his passes for 1,845 yards, 13 touchdowns and four interceptions. While the numbers are respectable, they have not quelled doubts among fans and analysts who point to a sputtering offensive line and a lack of rhythm with his receiving corps as factors limiting his effectiveness. Kubiak’s affirmation suggests that the coaching staff believes the quarterback’s performance, rather than any off‑field drama, will dictate his future.

The decision arrives at a critical juncture for the Raiders, who sit at 3‑3 and sit just outside the AFC West’s playoff picture. A win against the Jets would not only improve their record but also give the team momentum heading into a divisional showdown with the Kansas City Chiefs next week. Conversely, a loss could push Las Vegas further down the standings and intensify calls for a change at the helm. The Jets, meanwhile, are coming off a narrow defeat to the Buffalo Bills and will look to exploit the Raiders’ defensive vulnerabilities, particularly in the secondary, where they have allowed a 28.4‑yard average per pass attempt.

Analysts note that Cousins’ experience could be a double‑edged sword. On one hand, his poise in the pocket and ability to manage games have helped the Raiders stay competitive in close contests. On the other, his conservative approach may limit the offense’s explosiveness, especially against a Jets defense that has shown a propensity for forcing turnovers. The Raiders’ offensive coordinator, Shane Waldron, has hinted at incorporating more play‑action and deeper routes to stretch New York’s coverage, a strategy that could benefit from Cousins’ precise timing and strong arm.

The broader context of the decision also reflects a shift in the Raiders’ organizational philosophy. Since the hiring of Kubiak, the franchise has moved away from the “win‑or‑lose‑on‑the‑quarterback” mindset that defined much of the previous decade. Instead, the focus is on building a cohesive unit where the quarterback is supported by a solid offensive line, reliable receivers, and a versatile running game. By standing behind Cousins, the Raiders are signaling confidence in a longer‑term plan rather than a knee‑jerk reaction to short‑term setbacks.

Looking ahead, the outcome of Sunday’s contest will likely shape the narrative for the remainder of the season. A decisive victory could cement Cousins’ status as the franchise’s quarterback of choice and give the Raiders a platform to compete for a postseason berth. A disappointing performance, however, may reignite discussions about alternative options, including potential trades or a future draft investment. For now, the Raiders’ leadership has placed its trust in Cousins, betting that his veteran presence will guide the team through a pivotal stretch and keep Las Vegas in the hunt for AFC West supremacy.
